text:
maya: Heads-up — competitor X launched a low-cost, low-latency endpoint today. got a dozen inbound accounts already asking for 'same latency as theirs'. :eyes:

santhosh: saw that. their pitch is basically cheap micro-batches + aggressive quantization. noise for us unless customers start threatening to switch. any concrete asks?

lina: ACME pilot DMd asking if we can match latency for short prompts (<=64 tokens). they said price isn't as important as 50ms p99.

maya: ok — this is classic parity pull. want to discuss options: 1) match latency for short prompts (parity), 2) lean into reliability/quality (differentiate), 3) hybrid pricing/route (tiered fast path).

derek: we shouldn't throw away our SLOs. matching 50ms p99 everywhere is gonna cost a lot. but we can spec a 'fast-tail' plan: narrow scope (short prompts, specific models, quantized variants).

priya: propose launch criteria before we scope dev work:
- measurable p99 <= 60ms on short prompts (<=64 tokens) in staging
- <10% relative degredation in quality (eval set baseline)
- cost delta <= 1.5x current hosted per-token cost for fast-path

roshan: +1 on the checklist. add safety: fallback policy to standard model when hallucination risk > threshold.

lina: can product own the eval set? ACME gave a few call flows we can use. we'll need quantized model variants and a routing rule in API layer.

maya: rough timeline ask: is two sprints feasible for an MVP (routing + quantized model + canary)?

santhosh: dev estimate: quantized model onboarding 8-10d, routing changes + policy 3-4d, canary infra and observability 3d. total 2.5-3 weeks if we parallelize.

derek: ops note — we need per-route token/latency billing and per-route throttles for dedicated pools. that's extra scope if we want enterprise pricing parity.

priya: for prioritization, proposed RICE-like call:
- Reach: ~15 early-enterprise accounts (pilot)
- Impact: high for churn risk customers
- Confidence: medium (60%)
- Effort: 3 engineer sprints overall
=> recommend greenlight for MVP pilot with ACME and 2 other customers.

maya: risks?
- slides: increased cost, possible quality regressions, operational complexity.
- mitigation: narrow fast-path to short prompts + automatic fallback + telemetry for quality regressions.

roshan: telemetry hooks: record model variant, quantization level, prompt length bucket, latency p50/p95/p99, and semantic similarity score vs baseline. we'll need alerting on quality drift.

santhosh: engineering question — do we allow function-calling on fast quantized variants? might be unsupported initially. must call out explicitly in spec.

lina: spec draft items I'll put in a doc:
- scope: short prompts <=64 tokens, text-gen only, no function-calls
- models: curated quantized list (v1: q4_0 / q5_1)
- routing: request-level policy with header `x-fast-path: true` or server-side auto-route by token_count
- telemetry: per-request tag + quality eval backfill
- fallback: automatic <-> standard model when quality threshold breached

maya: sounds good. next steps: Lina to draft spec and launch criteria doc, Santhosh to validate dev estimates with infra, Derek to flag billing/ops impact, Priya to run go/no-go with GTM (ACME + 2 pilots).

deploy-bot: reminder — schedule a "fast-path parity" sync in #product for next Tue 10:00 if attendees confirm.

maya: tagging everyone: please react with :thumbsup: if you agree with the plan or comment differences by EOD Friday.

priya: +1 :thumbsup:

santhosh: +1

lina: will have draft by Thu EOD

roshan: noted

derek: +1

maya: thanks — we'll use the pilot to decide whether to expand fast-path beyond short prompts. if quality holds, we can scope multi-model support in Q3.
